rule: Label MERGE when the corpus establishes, via the surrounding sentence(s) in the cited source document(s), that the two surface forms refer to the SAME specific real-world entity -- either an identical name repeated across documents, a documented former/legal name (e.g. 'Apple Computer' for 'Apple Inc.'), or a person referred to first by full name and later by surname alone within the same corpus. Label REJECT when the two surface forms name DIFFERENT real-world entities, including cases that are lexically close or thematically related but not identical: a company is not its own product/service sub-brand (e.g. 'Apple' the company vs 'Apple Intelligence' the software feature), a chip variant is not a sibling chip variant (e.g. 'M5' vs 'M5 Pro'), a product line is not a different product line (e.g. 'MacBook Air' vs 'MacBook Pro'), and two distinct named people or organizations are never each other. Every surface string below is verified (at fixture-generation time, via the real graphrag.services.ingestion.parser.DocumentParser) to literally occur in its cited corpus/ source file -- none is an invented string.
